fullData.title: Adding Decimals on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo walks $0.4$ miles to the park, and then walks another $0.3$ miles to his friend's house. Use the number line to find the total distance Leo walks by adding $0.4$ and $0.3$. What is the total distance in miles?

fullData.solutionStrategy: Start at the park's position on the number line and count forward by three tenths.

steps.title: Locate starting point on number line

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, with a marker at 0.4 labeled Park.

labels.description: Leo starts at four tenths of a mile.
The location where Leo begins his second walk.

annotations.steps: Locate and mark 0.4 on the number line to show the first distance Leo walks.
annotations.strategy: I notice that starting at the first addend gives us our exact beginning location before adding more.
annotations.misconceptions: Starting at 0 instead of 0.4 because you forget that Leo already walked the first part of the trip.
annotations.connections: Plotting a decimal on a number line is just like plotting whole numbers, but the spaces are divided into tenths.
annotations.narrative: Find Leo's first stop at the point labeled Park at $0.4$ on the number line.

content.altText: A number line from 0.0 to 1.0 divided into tenths, showing three jumps of 0.1 forward starting from 0.4 and landing at 0.7.

labels.description: Leo's first distance to the park.
Count forward three tenths to the friend's house.

annotations.steps: Start at 0.4 on the number line and make three jumps of 0.1 forward to land at 0.7.
annotations.strategy: I notice that adding decimals is just like counting forward on a number line with whole numbers, but using smaller jumps of one-tenth.
annotations.misconceptions: A common error is counting the jumps instead of the tick marks, which can lead to starting your count on the wrong number and getting 0.6 instead of 0.7.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition to standard whole-number counting and prepares you for adding numbers with mixed units.
annotations.narrative: From $0.4$, count forward $3$ tick marks of $0.1$ each to land at the point labeled Friend's House at $0.7$. This shows $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$, so the total distance Leo walks is $0.7$ miles.

specs.title: Locate starting point on number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Understand how to represent the initial addend 0.4 as a starting location on a tenths-spaced number line.
specs.seedNotes: Plot a number line from 0 to 1 marked in increments of 0.1, highlighting the point at 0.4 labeled Park.

specs.title: Count forward by three tenths
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize addition of decimals as counting forward along tick marks to reach the total sum of 0.7.
specs.seedNotes: From 0.4, draw 3 successive jumps of 0.1 to reach 0.7 labeled Friend's House, connecting the visual to the equation 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

assignment.prompt: Leo already walked $0.4$ miles to the park. To add the next $0.3$ miles on the number line, which number should you start counting forward from?
assignment.rationale: Leo is already at the park at $0.4$ miles, so we start from $0.4$; starting at $0$ ignores the first leg of the walk, while $0.3$ is the distance to add rather than the starting position.
